rationale.campaign_length: 20 shared missions plus 2 exclusive missions, followed by the option to continue as B59.
rationale.colonization: The predecessor route has no colonial main line.
rationale.complexity: Military preparation, relations, and the shared Sway mechanics run in parallel.
rationale.dark_story: Its themes are autonomy and mediation.
rationale.difficulty: The community often considers it relatively approachable, but versions and player skill differ.
rationale.diplomacy: Relations with neighbors, Sway, and alliances are central.
rationale.early_pressure: A single city is constrained by Imperial princes and valley competition.
rationale.magic_artifice_intensity: The exclusive route is not built around spellcasting or artificing.
rationale.narrative_density: The old Damerian legion and postwar diplomacy provide a clear narrative thread.
rationale.tall_play: A one-province Free City whose exclusive missions develop capital manpower.
rationale.trade_economy: It shares valley trade missions, but is less maritime than Napesbay.
rationale.warfare: The officer and city-militia line provides defense; this is not purely peaceful.

identity.appearance: A republican Free City in 1444; one of four Luna River countries grouped in the scoring table.

successors.relationship: Can be formed after the shared finale and decision; this changes the Tag and mission tree.

description.text: Bluehart has always been surrounded by ambitious lords, eager to feast upon the riches of the Luna. Many a would-be conqueror have been turned away from our city, though not through the sword, but through the power of words. Our officials are experts in negotiating peace and reconciliation even with the most belligerent warlords, keeping our people safe from the horrors of combat.
description.text_en: Bluehart has always been surrounded by ambitious lords, eager to feast upon the riches of the Luna. Many a would-be conqueror have been turned away from our city, though not through the sword, but through the power of words. Our officials are experts in negotiating peace and reconciliation even with the most belligerent warlords, keeping our people safe from the horrors of combat.

description.text: Our city was originally founded as a legionary camp of the 21st Legion of Dameria, also known as the Legion XXI Hart. When the Republic fell to the Dragonwake, the former commander took control of the situation, allowing panicked civilians to flock to his protection and enforcing stability across the suddenly lawless frontier. In time he became known as The Hartlord, a paragon of peace and law, and when the Kingdom of Dameria rose from the ashes of the Republic, he readily submitted the new city of Bluehart to their rule, dying in his sleep as peacefully as he reigned. We hope to continue his legacy, acting as a force for goodwill despite whatever horrors wrack the lands around us.

description.text: With the exception of Port Munas, our city is the largest on the Luna River. A prime destination for trade flowing downstream from the Wexhills, Blueharter merchants have little trouble finding markets to trade with from the comfort of home.
description.text_en: With the exception of Port Munas, our city is the largest on the Luna River. A prime destination for trade flowing downstream from the Wexhills, Blueharter merchants have little trouble finding markets to trade with from the comfort of home.

description.text: The old legion camp is known as the Cymcestir, though it hasn't been used for its original wartime purposes for quite some time. Ever since the reign of The Hartlord, the compound has been used as a diplomatic complex, providing comforting accommodations for foreign dignitaries and secure rooms for tense negotiations.

description.text: Each member tracing direct lineage to the soldiers of the Legion XXI Hart, the Sons of the XXI are the brave sentinels of Bluehart, they alone are permitted to bear arms within city limits. They're said to fight with the ferocity of ten men each, determined to safeguard the city their ancestors fought for, that their children will grow up in, and that their descendants will continue to defend.

description.text: While turmoil brews around the city, none reaches past our city gates. Within the city is an atmosphere of tranquility, largely untouched by whatever calamity plagues the rest of the Empire.
description.text_en: While turmoil brews around the city, none reaches past our city gates. Within the city is an atmosphere of tranquility, largely untouched by whatever calamity plagues the rest of the Empire.

description.text: The Cymcestir was expanded and converted into the Olóiegéanur Academy in 1604 as a result of simmering tensions within the fabric of Anbennar. The professors of the establishment find great gratification in training the next generation of statesmen and emissaries to act as agents of peace, ready to mend broke bridges across the Empire and assist in healing the wounds of the past.

Tomás of Vallusna, ‘The Statesman’

description.text:
“The imitation of style necessitates the imitation of form, and therefore of function. When we build a colonnade inspired by the formal markets of Old Dameria, we are inspired also by the conversation held along that colonnade, the type of life enabled by the structure we seek to recreate. The rhetorical tradition, the vibrant public life, even the raucous protest – all are made possible by the decision, made once again, to build space for them.”
Saman of Fowlbarn, ‘The Life Of Stone’

description.text:
“Even in those realms which had not subordinated their government to an association of guild-backed aldermen, the Guild had been the fundamental unit of urban life in the Eastern Dameshead long before Pashainé’s emergence as a coherent state.

This had three major consequences. First, the codification of a sort of corporate democracy, a belief that society was best forged under a competing set of mutually-exerted pressures, by groups representing collectives of the population - even if these were subject to a monarch or a so-called ’Executive Guild’. Second, an emphasis on economic prosperity, the brass tacks ‘shopkeeper diplomacy’ for which Pashainé became notorious. Third, a relentless focus on urbanisation and the vertical integration of industry.”
Silvard Dove, ‘An Economic History of Cannor’

description.text:
“The poet Milian said that the Pashainéy is uniquely noble, having inherited the bravery of his Vernman father and the dignity of his Damerian mother. As a second daughter, I seem to have been left with the libido and stubbornness.”
Genaia ‘Geni’ Cadesna sina Bellacaire, ‘Memoirs Of A Fallen Countess’

description.text:
“Consider the conflict between Corinism and the Court which had so split the Valley. Consider, then, an unusually literate and engaged populace with a political impetus to see theological ruptures healed. Consider finally the Ravelian Lodge, which in its structure mimics the voluntary association basis of the guild. No population on Halann was more ready to embrace not merely the articles of belief but the basic organisational structure of Ravelianism.”
Leande Bellac, ‘Apologetics’

description.text:
“Over the course of the eighteenth century, the slowly aggregating impact of the Verdancy became more and more clear across the entire Luna watershed. Land which had once been among the most fertile in Cannor gave harvest perhaps once in two years, while the concomitant soil pollution devastated the Valley’s few remaining natural forests. The result was an exodus of the population from the countryside and an even greater urbanisation of Pashainé, inadvertently birthing a contentious café and street culture; this would dominate the labour politics of the following hundred years, erupting again and again into civil unrest. You will find few along the Valley who have much to say in praise of Camir Silmuna, but our land is indelibly marked by his legacy.”
Lucas síl Bellacaire, The History of the Lilac River, Vol. II

description.text:
“Do not fear death, my people. Fear nothing which you do in the company of brave souls; fear nothing which you do among your fellow citizens! We live in the time of the Mage-Emperors – in the era of the staff – and its power seems absolute. But we know these mages can die.

We knew it three hundred years ago, when the discipline of the fusillade first began to rival the arc of the fireball. We knew it two hundred years ago, when first we learned of that glorious substance, then accessible only so very far away, which could countermand their unearned gifts. And we know it now – now that their ritual of growth, their promise of endless harvest, has wrought a desolate steppe where once there was only verdant life. It is what they do! Addle the land, poison the water, wreck the bountiful Halann we share for the slightest chance at a lonely throne.

Hear me! It’s true – we may die today. But we die together, while they die alone.”
Carric of Paredocks, Final Address

player_overview.avoid_if: Players who want to ignore neighboring relations and solve the opening through large-scale early conquest.
player_overview.how_it_plays: First stabilize diplomacy and manpower, then use Imperial relations, Sway, and limited wars to integrate the Luna.
player_overview.overview: You start as Bluehart, an East Damerian Free City. The Hartlord and the 21st Legion left more than a martial tradition: the city prefers persuasion and uses its barracks and envoys to preserve autonomy. Stabilize the neighbours, develop officers and the citizen militia, then use Luna River influence diplomacy to guide the cities toward Pashainé.
player_overview.recommended_for: Players who favor diplomatic negotiation, small republics, and steady military preparation.
signature_features: Two exclusive missions connect Damerian relations, officers, and the city militia.
The old legion camp in the ideas contrasts sharply with the diplomatic-reputation theme.
20 shared missions take a one-province Free City toward an alliance and a formable country.
player_overview.tagline: Inherit the Damerian legion memory, use military preparation as a shield, and preserve a Luna Free City through negotiation.

reasons: The distinctive history of the Damerian 21st Legion and the Hartlord
The combination of diplomacy and military preparation
Often considered the smoothest opening among the four by player experience
warnings: Do not present the 1604 academy as an existing 1444 starting building

values.rationale: The national ideas and missions emphasize mediation, urban autonomy, restoring relations, and avoiding domination by great powers; defensive military preparation serves to protect the community rather than to conquer.
